summary: Suggests a schedule for implementing the IP network number allocation plan described in RFC 1366. It was replaced by RFC 1467.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1367 proposes dates for carrying out the IP address allocation plan in RFC 1366. The schedule was intended to help prepare for an Internet address aggregation mechanism.

questions: when did class c block allocation begin
subtitle: A proposed timeline for putting an IP address allocation plan into practice.

tldr.problem: The IP network number allocation plan needed a practical schedule that could support deployment of an address aggregation mechanism.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC proposes four dated steps for registry criteria, a schedule review, block allocation, and expected availability of aggregation.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1367 is informational and has been obsoleted by RFC 1467.

today: RFC 1367 is informational and has been obsoleted by RFC 1467.

sections.title: Purpose of the Schedule
sections.content:
This memo suggests when to implement the IP network number allocation plan described in RFC 1366. It says that the schedule is meant to support deployment of an address aggregation mechanism and help reduce Internet router forwarding table size while managing IP address space.

The proposed schedule assumes that the aggregation mechanism will be available in the Internet by mid-1993. The memo presents its dates as targets for discussion and community agreement.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo sets target dates for putting the address plan in place. It assumes that a way to combine address routes will be available by mid-1993.

sections.title: Initial Steps and Review
sections.content:
On 31 October 1992, the initial criteria for regional address registries were to take effect, and IANA was to accept applications from prospective registries. Class A numbers were described as practically impossible to obtain. Class B numbers would continue only when reasonably justified, with a block of Class C numbers preferred where possible; Class C allocation would follow the RFC 1366 plan.

On 14 February 1993, the schedule was to be reviewed and adjusted if necessary.
sections.plainLanguage: The first date starts regional registry criteria and tighter handling of Class B numbers. A later date is set aside to review and adjust the plan.

sections.title: Block Allocation and Aggregation
sections.content:
Starting 15 April 1993, the Internet Registry was to allocate all networks according to the addressing plan, using appropriately sized blocks of Class C numbers. Class B numbers would be difficult to obtain and issued only when justified.

6 June 1993 was the expected date for an address aggregation mechanism to be available in the Internet. The RFC describes this as a proposed schedule, not a report that the mechanism had already been deployed.
sections.plainLanguage: The plan moves network allocations to sized blocks of Class C numbers in April. The memo expects address aggregation to be available in June.

references.text: Gerich, E., "Guidelines for Management of IP Address Space", RFC 1366, October 1992.
